name: Crystal Pepsi
blurb: PepsiCo's clear, caffeine-free cola of 1992–93, brought back for short runs since 2015
title: Crystal Pepsi: What It Was, Why It Failed and Its Comebacks
description: Crystal Pepsi was a clear, caffeine-free cola PepsiCo launched in 1992 and dropped by early 1994. Short re-releases followed in 2015–2017 and a 2022 giveaway.
answer: Crystal Pepsi was a clear, caffeine-free cola that PepsiCo test-marketed in April 1992 and sold across the US from December 1992. After a strong start the clear-drink fad faded, production stopped in late 1993 and the last deliveries went out in early 1994. PepsiCo has since brought it back only briefly, through a 2015 sweepstakes, limited store runs in 2016 and 2017, and a 2022 anniversary giveaway.

body: Crystal Pepsi looked like soda water but was meant to taste like cola. PepsiCo left out the caramel color and the caffeine and pitched it in the early-1990s spirit of "clear" as pure and light. It had 134 calories per 12-ounce serving against regular Pepsi's 154, and it was reported to taste less acidic than regular Pepsi. A Diet Crystal Pepsi followed in August 1992.

The launch was loud: a $40 million campaign that included about $7 million of Super Bowl advertising, with a commercial set to Van Halen's "Right Now" premiering during Super Bowl XXVII on January 31, 1993. In its first year Crystal Pepsi took about 1% of US soft drink sales, roughly $474 million.

head: Year
What happened
rows: April 13: test markets in Dallas, Providence, Salt Lake City and Colorado; nationwide US launch in December
January: arrives in Canada and stars in a Super Bowl ad; production ends late in the year
Final deliveries early in the year; a citrus-cola reformulation, Crystal From Pepsi, appears briefly
After an online fan petition, PepsiCo gives Crystal Pepsi away in a holiday sweepstakes
Limited store run in Canada from July 11 and in the US from August 8
Another limited US run from August 14 in 20-ounce bottles (suggested price $1.79), billed by PepsiCo as "one last limited time"
30th anniversary: in the US, 300 winners of a January giveaway get six bottles each, with no store sales

body: Novelty carried the first months, but sales faded as the clear-drink trend of the early 1990s wore off. Coca-Cola also answered with Tab Clear in December 1992; its marketing chief later described it as a deliberate "kamikaze" product meant to kill off both clear colas. David Novak, the PepsiCo executive credited with the concept, later called Crystal Pepsi the best idea he ever had and the worst executed.

Not as a regular product. Since 1994 Crystal Pepsi has existed only in short, announced runs and giveaways; the 2022 anniversary bottles in the US were prizes rather than a store release. PepsiCo itself called the 2017 run the last time on shelves, and it has not announced a permanent return as of 2026.

faq.q: When did Crystal Pepsi come out?
faq.a: It was test-marketed from April 13, 1992 and went nationwide in the US in December 1992.
No. The original Crystal Pepsi was caffeine-free and had no caramel coloring, which is what made it clear.
PepsiCo has not announced a permanent return. It has brought the drink back only for limited runs, most recently a 2022 anniversary giveaway.
